$comment: Normative (FLR-ADR-006). The `default` keywords here are exactly the constant defaults of 5.1's Junction table; the reference canonicalizer reads them as its table of constant defaults (9.2 step 1).
title: Junction
description: 5.1: a node of a level's wall graph — a point on a level where walls and separators start and end. Every junction MUST reference a level (FS-CORE-1.3.2). It has only the members of its table (FS-CORE-1.4.1). That no two junctions on a level share a position (FS-CORE-5.1.1) is an invariant (FS-INV-101), not checked here.

level.description: 1.3, 5.1: a reference to the level the junction is on. Always present.

position.description: 5.1: where the junction is, in plan. Always present.

join.description: 5.1, 5.8: how the walls meeting here are cut.

option.description: 19.2: a reference to the option this junction is in. Absent: it is in no option, and so in every design.

name.description: 1.4: a human-readable label, 1–200 characters. Absent by default.

join.title: Join override
join.description: 5.8: how the walls meeting at the junction are cut — the default mitre, or a butt join naming one or two walls that run through. Whether a butt join applies to its junction (FS-CORE-5.8.1 to 5.8.3) is an invariant (FS-INV-111), not checked here.

oneOf.title: Butt join
oneOf.description: 5.8: { "kind": "butt", "through": [W] } or { "kind": "butt", "through": [W1, W2] } — one or two walls run through the junction and every other edge stops against them.

through.title: Through walls
through.description: 5.8: references to the one or two walls that run through the junction.
